Barcode match in >=2 sources is only partly met (jpc.de and amazon.de list 4099964172904 and Thalia shows the EAN). Independent database confirming the barcode is missing -> NOT MET. 4: barcode match in only one source? Multiple shop pages confirm EAN; but the database match is iTunes (digital) and the physical CD match rests on shops. Level 4 MET: barcode match in at least one source with format CD and artist consistent. Competing editions: Discogs 2024 release (barcode 4099964124866, CD, 2×CD) has a different barcode and possibly different tracklist, and iTunes 2026 edition is a different year; the 2024 Discogs release has no tracklist durations and is a different barcode so it is not an exact barcode competitor, yet the title-matching edition is a different catalogue entry. edition.summary: Barcode 4099964172904 is matched by several shop pages (jpc, Amazon, Thalia) for a 2×CD in the right format and artist, but no independent database confirms the EAN, and a Discogs 2024 edition with a different barcode competes.

sources.check: 4: database + specialised collector site: MET partially (iTunes database, Discogs database for a different edition). Two independent database entries with differing details: iTunes album and Discogs release 33835569 differ (different barcode, year 2024, different title). But the Discogs entry is a different edition, so it does not confirm this edition. Database + shop: jpc.de and Amazon are shops. sources.summary: The main confirming database is iTunes (digital), while Discogs is a different 2024 edition, and the shop pages are the only physical-CD sources, so sources are one good database plus shops.

concerns: Discogs 2024 release 33835569 (barcode 4099964124866, 2xCD) is a different edition and its tracklist was not compared against the 40-track result.
iTunes album 1824661315 is a digital catalogue entry; not a physical confirmation of the CD.
